A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentBreeder research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithm, and appendices support comparison despite changes in formatting and organization.

before.justification: v3 reports original scaffold-search experiments in blue, red, and capability-only modes, including benchmark results and a multi-objective ablation.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and additionally reports HV indicators comparing seed and discovered scaffold populations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the three optimization modes, mutation and crossover procedures, clustering, prompts, and example scaffold remain substantively unchanged. Section 4.1 adds clarification of existing balanced sampling.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DROP, MMLU, GPQA, SaladData's Attack Enhanced subset, and TruthfulQA. The inverted safety objective and represented tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The seven hand-designed seed comparators remain in the blue and red comparisons. The capability-only experiment retains the same seed and ADAS-discovered scaffold comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 adds the HV indicator as a test-set evaluation metric for the existing blue and red experiments. Previously reported generation budgets, sample counts, models, and accuracy/F1 evaluations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The capability-only ablation and helpfulness-based reward-hacking analysis are retained. The HV tables add aggregate performance reporting without introducing a new ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: The retained results preserve their confidence intervals, bootstrap description, and run information. The new checklist reiterates uncertainty-reporting claims but documents no additional independent runs, random seeds, or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: New Tables 1 and 3 report HV results; for example, blue-mode GPQA has seed/discovered values of 0.219064/0.247536. The red discovered value is malformed as 0.0.602547. All numerical entries in v3 Tables 1–3 match v4 Tables 2, 4, and 5, and the original plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The Pareto definitions and mathematical substance remain unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and v4 introduces no mathematical definition or derivation for its added HV reporting.

C1.justification: The attack, defense, and evaluation contributions remain unchanged, as do the abstract and conclusion claims about safety improvement, retained capability, and discovering vulnerable scaffolds.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets red-mode optimization as outer misalignment: a misspecified reward function incentivizes unsafe behavior while pursuing beneficial objectives. Existing limitations, reward-hacking interpretations, and dual-use discussion are retained.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies that positive validation samples are baseline-CoT successes and that best-scaffold selection maximizes capability plus safety after excluding reward hacking. Figure captions identify validation results. It also updates the code link and adds conflicting MIT and Non-Commercial licensing statements; the PDFs do not establish the actual license.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning relative to ADAS, evolutionary scaffold design, and multi-agent safety remain unchanged. Numbered citations replace author-year citations without changing research coverage.

P1.justification: v4 makes targeted explanatory edits, revises title and author/header text, reorganizes appendix material, and adds a NeurIPS checklist. Most scientific prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the empirical displays: it adds two HV tables, moves Figures 2–3 into the main experiments, and moves the capability-only table into Appendix B. NeurIPS formatting replaces the earlier template, table shading changes, and several side-by-side captions become captions below their displays.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency about sampling, scaffold selection, and red-mode interpretation, and adds quantitative Pareto summaries absent from v3. However, HV remains undefined, the new red-mode table contains a malformed value, and the checklist introduces conflicting licensing statements. With the underlying results unchanged, these documentation gains and new reporting problems leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
